description: Before March 2026 the member had paid $400 out of pocket and met the full $150 in-network deductible, and the cover shows the deductible met. Claim 1 is a dermatology visit with a skin biopsy; the biopsy, a 20% coinsurance service, is charged the $150 deductible again plus 20% of the rest. Claim 2 (lab tests) is correct. A careful reviewer should conclude the deductible was already met, so the member owes only 20% of the biopsy's plan-approved amount.

sources.what: A PPO with a deductible must have a single one; this plan's $150 in-network deductible applies once a year to coinsurance services, then 20% (note C1)
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.101(d)(1), Requirements relating to basic benefits (single deductible for local PPO plans; other services may be waived from it), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.101; eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(b)(2), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111

sources.what: Medicare Advantage plans set their own deductibles and cost sharing each year, and the evidence of coverage says what you pay
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Understanding Medicare Advantage Plans (CMS Product No. 12026), https://www.medicare.gov/publications/12026-understanding-medicare-advantage-plans.pdf

sources.what: A Medicare Advantage plan mails an EOB each month you visit a provider, summarizing your claims and costs
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Checking the status of a claim, https://www.medicare.gov/providers-services/claims-appeals-complaints/claims/check-status
